description: Hand-labeled Python verdict corpus: one-line edits in small authored Python projects, one subject per test library, each labeled with what the project's own tests actually discriminate, so ripr's Python verdicts can be scored as false actionable, false exposed, false silent, abstained, or ideal.
label_method: For each case the edit was applied to a scratch copy of the whole authored project, the project's own test command (pytest, with Hypothesis where a subject uses it, or python3 -m unittest, recorded on the case) was run to confirm the edit keeps tests green (behavior_preserving_rewrite) or to record whether it breaks them (behavior_change, where the edit is its own single mutant), and each listed mutant of the edited line was applied on top and the same command run. A mutant counts as detected (`tests_failed`) when the test command fails after the code loads; no recorded failure is an import or syntax error. Each mutant was reviewed by hand for equivalence. Truth is derived from the count of mutants with tests_failed: all is discriminated, none is not_discriminated, otherwise partially_discriminated.
verdict_projection: Only candidate_current findings on the anchor file and line count, plus, when the anchor is a plain `let name = init;` or `let mut name = init;`, candidate_current findings in the anchor file whose binding_predicate_relation evidence names that binding with init as its new initializer (the RIPR-SPEC-0157 retarget). exposed is credited; a named static_limit_kind or a no_static_path, infection_unknown, propagation_unknown or static_unknown class is limited; any other class (weakly_exposed, reachable_unrevealed) is a gap. A gap on the line outranks credit, and credit outranks a limit. No anchored finding is silent. The per-finding reading mirrors crates/ripr/src/output/human/triage.rs; the line-level precedence is this corpus's own policy.
non_claims: Rates describe this corpus only; they are not a population estimate for Python code or for ripr in general.
Every subject is authored to cover a test-library oracle or reach rule; the rates describe those cells, not real-world Python tests.
Truth comes from the listed mutants, not from exhaustive mutation; a discriminated label means every listed mutant made the test command fail.
The harness does not run mutation testing, the Python test runners, or any network access.
